definitions.E26:
Understood—we’ll keep **Accounting** as the subject.

## Bachelor of Accounting

- **Credential:** Bachelor’s degree  
- **School:** School of Business + Media  
- **Campus:** Burnaby Campus  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Study options:** Full-time day stream or part-time Flexible Learning  
- **Program status:** Active  

The program is designed to provide an academic credential leading toward the **CPA designation**. It may also support progression to a Master of Professional Accounting or MBA. CPA alignment is academic preparation only; completing the program does not itself award CPA certification or licensure.

### Academic requirements

The stored program requirements include:

- **60.0 academic credits**
- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the Advanced Technical Specialty pool**
- **36.0 General Education credits**
  - **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing**
  - **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**
  - Additional General Education credits under the published category requirements

The Advanced Technical Specialty pool includes:

- **ACCG 6310 — Auditing and Assurance**
- **FMGT 7121 — Advanced Accounting**
- **FMGT 7210 — Advanced Management Accounting**
- **FMGT 7310 — Advanced Auditing**
- **FMGT 7410 — Taxation of Close Corporations**
- **FMGT 7510 — Advanced Finance**
- **FMGT 7520 — Business Valuation**
- **FMGT 7910 — The Business Environment**
- **FMGT 8121 — Contemporary Issues in Accounting**
- **FMGT 8610 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 1**
- **FMGT 8620 — Independent Technical Studies Abroad 2**
- **FMGT 8920 — Case Writing Fundamentals**

You choose **seven courses** from that approved pool; the courses are not all cumulative requirements.

Optional work terms, available to eligible full-time domestic students, are:

- **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1**
- **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**

These optional work terms do not form part of the 60-credit academic requirement. They are unavailable to international students.

### Admission information

The stored admission requirements include:

- A BCIT Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma, or an equivalent external diploma assessed individually
- Minimum diploma GPA of **70%**
- English Studies 12 at **67%**, or equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two in the 62%–65% range
- A signed departmental pre-entry assessment and any assigned bridging or upgrading

The subject-sequence and pre-entry assessment requirements require institutional confirmation.

The program page states that international applicants may apply, subject to study-permit and other institutional or immigration requirements. Final PGWP decisions are made by IRCC.

definitions.E1:
## Bachelor of Accounting overview

The **Bachelor of Accounting** is an active, in-person program at the **Burnaby Campus**, offered through either full-time daytime study or part-time Flexible Learning.

Students complete **60 academic credits**, including:

- **FMGT 8911 — Strategic Performance Management**
- **Seven courses chosen from the approved technical elective pool**
- **36 General Education credits**, including **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing** and **LIBS 7002 — Applied Ethics**

Optional work terms include **FMGT 7610 — Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 — Workplace Education Workterm 2**; they are available only to eligible full-time domestic students and are not part of the 60-credit academic requirement.

The program provides academic preparation toward pathways such as the CPA designation, a Master of Professional Accounting, or an MBA; it does not itself award professional certification.

- **In person** at the **Burnaby Campus**
- Available through **full-time day studies** or **part-time Flexible Learning**

If you have an external diploma, equivalency is assessed individually and bridging may be required. If you are an international applicant, a valid BCIT study permit is required before starting, and the optional work terms are unavailable.

definitions.E8:
For the **Applied Computing Master of Science**, admission is competitive and has a two-step process.

### Step 1: Meet the entrance requirements

All applicants need:

- **English proficiency:** Graduate Studies English Studies 12 with at least **67%**, or an equivalent qualification. Equivalency may require confirmation.
- **One of these entry routes:**
  - **Standard entry:** A bachelor’s degree in computer science or an equivalent field, with a minimum **2.8/4.0 GPA (70%)** across the final 30 undergraduate credits.
  - **Alternate entry:** A bachelor’s degree in another discipline, with a minimum **3.0/4.0 GPA (73%)** across the final 30 credits, plus significant computing knowledge through formal education and/or work experience. This route also requires a pre-entry assessment; bridging courses may be required.
- **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire**
- **Two references**, submitted directly to the admissions committee.
- Applicants with post-secondary studies outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand require a comprehensive **ICES credential evaluation**; other Canadian evaluation services may be considered.

### Step 2: Department review

Complete applications are reviewed and ranked competitively by the Graduate Program Committee. Relevant industry experience is preferred, but the stored requirements do not specify a minimum amount.

definitions.E23: The Master of Science Degree in Applied Computing gives you in-depth computing knowledge to solve complex real-world problems across industries and sectors. Through an interdisciplinary and rigorous full-time curriculum, you’ll be equipped to provide technical leadership in a professional setting or pursue further academic study. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing About the program Applied computing integrates information technology, computer science, and industry. You’ll take courses in core computing, and you will have the opportunity to work in an application area in another discipline. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how advanced computing, tools, and computational methods can be applied in practice to overcome challenges and create efficiencies. The program employs a cohort model, with the same group in all courses. This allows you to work through the program together, sharing your experience and expertise and building industry connections that will last long after you graduate 1 intake: September 4 15-week terms, normally completed over two academic years full time First year with two terms , delivered in-person, including: Algorithm analysis Human-centered Computing Machine Learning (ML) & Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Science Cybersecurity Research methods Second year on thesis path or internship & project path Based on BCIT Burnaby Campus, and possibly the Downtown Campus or field locations where appropriate. You’ll be uniquely qualified to apply your knowledge and skills in various areas, such as: computational science rehabilitation engineering building science biotechnology autonomous vehicles sustainability smart micro-grids social impacts of technology network security an approved project area of your choosing based on your professional background See the Program Details to learn more. Who it’s for This degree might be for you if you: Are inspired to maximize the societal benefit of computing by solving real-world issues Would like to apply your skills in industry after graduation, but might also consider applying for a PhD Are looking for a cohort-based program where you’ll work with other students to share problem-solving skills and approaches, as you would in a work setting Have an applied problem you believe could be improved through computing Would like to study with computing faculty, application experts outside of computing, and industry partners Students will also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to gain additional knowledge in a specific application area. Please review the Entrance Requirements to learn more. What grads can do Provide technical leadership for software/system development teams Demonstrate deep, critical knowledge and understanding of advanced topics in computing science Analyze how computing systems and software can be used in practical applications and interdisciplinary fields Design, develop, and implement innovative solutions to industry problems with consideration to relevant ethical, social and environmental issues Explain and advocate for applied computing solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences in both business and academic settings See the Graduating & Jobs page to learn more. Next up Entrance Requirements
definitions.E25: This degree focuses on Applied Computing, which is fundamentally related to applying computing technology and computational methods to derive solutions to complex practical problems. Course work will emphasize current issues in industry, case studies, and applied research projects. This program offers you a chance to work with an interdisciplinary and diverse team of academic supervisors that may include faculty from Computing, faculty from an application domain, as well as industry practitioners. You’ll also have the opportunity to undertake directed studies with a supervisor in a different department to explore a specific application area. For more information about faculty, visit the Faculty, Advisors & Staff page. Applied research is fundamental to the program. Two paths are offered, diverging in second year: Thesis Path – Path 1: complete a thesis project and defend it in your second year. You’ll need to demonstrate originality in the application of your knowledge, either through new publishable research, or a novel solution to an existing practical problem. This is the best path if you’re interested in possibly pursuing a future Ph.D. Project & Internship Path – Path 2: a one-semester research project with a one-semester internship, which may be paid or unpaid. The internship will involve an external company or a BCIT lab where you can learn how advanced computing techniques are applied to solve interdisciplinary problems. The research project may be done in collaboration with the sponsor from the internship, providing added value in terms of practical utility. Students will also complete a 3-credit special topics course, covering emerging areas in Applied Computing, such as Quantum Computing, Generative AI, or Deep Learning. Both paths will require students to: examine literature in a related discipline, recognize gaps and limitations in existing technologies and processes, organize and plan their approach, and demonstrate competence in applying advanced techniques to solve problems. In both paths, students will present a written argument that addresses a complex problem in applied computing. Did you miss our Info Session? Please see the recording from October 2024: BCIT Master of Science in Applied Computing | Info Session Program length Two years, full-time. The maximum time to complete this program is five years. Grading Students will be required to maintain a minimum average of 70% across all courses in the program before starting their thesis or research project. Student progress through the program will be monitored by the supervisor, in consultation with the Program Head. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs
